record.original_question: Find new combinatorial invariants of flat virtual knots, and determine richer algebraic structures that can detect flat virtual-knot phenomena beyond mod 2 linking numbers despite the fact that the flat biquandle algebra is isomorphic to the Weyl algebra and has no non-trivial finite-dimensional representations.

evidence.quote: Flat virtual knots, also known as virtual strings [64, 214], are difficult to classify. Find new combinatorial invariants of flat virtual knots.
We would like to know more about the flat biquandle algebra. This algebra is isomorphic to the Weyl algebra [55] and has no (non-trivial) finite dimensional representations.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A flat virtual knot (equivalently, a virtual string) is an equivalence class of virtual knot diagrams under the generalized Reidemeister moves together with the relation that identifies each classical crossing with its mirror (i.e., over/under information is forgotten, while virtual crossings remain distinct from flat classical crossings). Two flat virtual knots are known to be distinguished, in part, by mod 2 linking numbers between components and by the flat biquandle algebra, which is the unital associative algebra generated by two invertible elements A and B subject to the single relation
   A^{-1} B^{-1} A B - B^{-1} A B = B A^{-1} B^{-1} A - A.
This algebra is isomorphic to the Weyl algebra and admits no nontrivial finite-dimensional representations.

Problem. Construct new combinatorial invariants of flat virtual knots, and identify richer algebraic structures (for example, modules, quotients, deformations, or representation-theoretic data associated with the flat biquandle algebra / Weyl algebra) capable of distinguishing flat virtual knots that cannot be separated by mod 2 linking numbers, in spite of the absence of nontrivial finite-dimensional representations of the flat biquandle algebra.
artifact.status_search_result: The classification and invariant theory of flat virtual knots remains an active and open area. Recent works (e.g., parity biquandle invariants and virtual biquandle cocycle quiver representations from 2016–2025) develop new invariants but do not resolve the broader problem of finding combinatorial invariants of flat virtual knots beyond mod 2 linking numbers, nor extract a complete algebraic invariant from the flat biquandle (Weyl) algebra.

status_evidence.title: Virtual Biquandle Cocycle Quiver Representations
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) construction of new biquandle-based invariants of virtual knots, indicating ongoing development of invariants in this area.
status_evidence.claim: Research on biquandle-based invariants for virtual and flat virtual knots is ongoing, with new invariants still being introduced.

status_evidence.title: Parity biquandle invariants of virtual knots
status_evidence.snippet: Develops parity biquandle invariants which extend biquandle invariants for virtual knots.
status_evidence.claim: New invariants beyond the classical biquandle continue to be developed but no complete invariant of flat virtual knots is known.

status_evidence.title: Weyl Algebras and Knots
status_evidence.snippet: The flat biquandle algebra is isomorphic to the Weyl algebra and has no nontrivial finite-dimensional representations.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the algebraic obstruction noted in the problem statement.
